values.altText: An email draft with comment bubbles from two teammates

values.text:
Once the editing basics are in place, the next questions are usually about working together.

If your customers share content, they expect to leave feedback in context, see what changed and try things without fear. That’s what separates a basic embedded editor from a great one.
With Blockwise, you can add collaboration as your product grows.
Let people leave feedback inside the editor, so reviews happen in context.
Several people can work on the same message at once.
Undo, redo and version history take the worry out of shared work.
Let your users decide who can do what in each project.

As your product matures, these features also make a natural basis for pricing tiers. You can choose which features each plan includes.

Many teams start simple and grow. The good news: you won’t need to rebuild your editor to add more later.
